## Natural history notes

A small to medium-sized owlet moth characterized by mottled brown to grayish forewings with fine wavy lines and a darker blackish patch or shading near the wing tip. In Florida, it is found in forests, hammocks, pine flatwoods, forest edges, parks, and other wooded or semi-wooded habitats where suitable host plants and resting cover occur. Adults are mostly nocturnal and may come to lights, while the caterpillars feed on plant material and serve as part of the broader food web for birds, bats, spiders, and other insect-eating animals.
